rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Summary of 01 ecosystem ecology concept of ecology biotic and abiotic factors species interactions concept of ecosystem structural and functional aspects of pond and forest ecosystem. Ecology studies the interactions between organisms and their environment. Biotic (living) and abiotic (non-living) factors shape every ecosystem. Species interact through mutualism, commensalism, parasitism, predation, and competition.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Ecosystem = Biotic (producers + consumers + decomposers) + Abiotic (light, water, soil, gases)
Species interactions: mutualism (+/+), commensalism (+/0), parasitism (+/-), predation (+/-), competition (-/-)
Energy flow: Sun → Producer → Primary consumer → Secondary consumer → ... → Heat (unidirectional)

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Ecology: study of organism-environment interactions.  ·  Biotic (living) vs abiotic (non-living) factors.  ·  Species interactions: mutualism, commensalism, parasitism, predation, competition.  ·  Ecosystem = biotic + abiotic; types: aquatic + terrestrial.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: A single hectare of a tropical forest can contain 100+ tree species.  ·  The sun is the primary energy source of almost all ecosystems.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Detailed notes on 01 ecosystem ecology concept of ecology biotic and abiotic factors species interactions concept of ecosystem structural and functional aspects of pond and forest ecosystem within the ecology unit.  ·  Ecology: the study of the interactions between organisms and their environment (biotic + abiotic).  ·  Biotic factors: living components (plants, animals, microorganisms); Abiotic factors: non-living (light, temperature, water, soil, pH, gases).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Nutrient cycling  ·  Pond/forest ecosystems  ·  In nature an organism does not exist in isolation, it is associated with organisms of its own and of different kinds as well as with the physical environment.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: If the organism is plant, it depends for growth on the aerial environment for light, temperature and carbon dioxide, on the soil environment for inorganic nutrients and water.  ·  If it is an animal it depends on the plants for food and shelter.  ·  If it is a microorganism it depend on the dead organic matter from plants and animals for its food, and releases the nutrients tied in the organic matter for the reuse of plants.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Thus, there are continuous interactions among the organisms and between the organisms and the habitat resulting into an integrated, functional unit.  ·  Structural: producers, consumers, decomposers; trophic levels.  ·  Functional: energy flow (unidirectional) + nutrient cycling (biogeochemical).
